title: California Code of Civil Procedure section 996.480 - Surety payment once the principal's liability is established
claims: Section 996.480(a) applies if the nature and extent of the liability of the principal is established by final judgment of a court and the time for appeal has expired or, if an appeal is taken, the appeal is finally determined and the judgment is affirmed.

Section 996.480(a)(1) provides that in that event a surety may make payment on a bond without awaiting enforcement of the bond, and the amount of the bond is reduced to the extent of any payment made by the surety in good faith.

Section 996.480(a)(2) provides that if the beneficiary makes a claim for payment on a bond given in an action or proceeding after the principal's liability is so established and the surety fails to make payment, the surety is liable for costs incurred in obtaining a judgment against the surety, including a reasonable attorney's fee, and interest on the judgment from the date of the claim, notwithstanding Section 996.470.
Section 996.480(b) provides that partial payment of a claim by a surety shall not be considered satisfaction of the claim and the beneficiary may enforce the liability on the bond.
notes: Fetched 2026-09-30 from the publisher's own site and read in full. Part of the Bond and Undertaking Law (Code of Civil Procedure 995.010 onward). By section 995.020 the chapter yields where the statute requiring a particular bond prescribes a different rule or is inconsistent, so this section is a default rather than the rule for every bond. Added by Stats. 1982, Ch. 998.
